correctness.rationale: A complete symbolic proof classifies all accepted binary positions as 1(1|00)*, decomposes lexicographic suffix lists into 00L_{j-2} and 1L_{j-1}, computes the interface difference, and counts each distinct gap via Fibonacci composition prefixes. It handles the zero-position and binary-length boundaries separately; the terminating one at each dyadic cutoff removes censoring. The limit weights follow from Binet asymptotics and total mass one. The packaged verify.py run was actually performed and passed 262144 direct terms and dyadic cutoff formulas through K=18. It is corroboration, not an infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The main comparison is Merta 2018, where an exact accepted-position recursion and a coarse unbounded-zero-run statement are given; no complete run-length spectrum or dyadic Fibonacci frequency formula is supplied. Merta Theorem 4.6 is about a distinct formal-inverse sequence. The OEIS table/generator determines individual positions but does not state a complete run-length/frequency theorem. A nearby general automatic-word paper studies repetition factorizations instead. Targeted semantic searches and prior-claim examination yielded no explicit or dominating theorem; an inaccessible/unindexed equivalent remains a risk.
residual_risks: An unindexed equivalent formula for Baum–Sweet run gaps or an overlooked sequence-database difference entry may exist.
The result does not prove convergence for arbitrary cutoff lengths, only for dyadic prefix lengths.
Merta’s accepted-position recursion is essential known background; the present result claims the derived global spectrum and exact multiscale multiplicities, not that recurrence.

value.rationale: A complete unbounded family of allowed maximal zero-run lengths is a structurally motivated combinatorics-on-words invariant, substantially more informative than the known existence of arbitrarily long runs. Exact dyadic Fibonacci multiplicities and a full limiting distribution distinguish common short gaps from a geometric tail, and precisely exclude all other lengths. Binary-power prefixes are natural for a 2-automatic word and all their runs are complete.
